messages:
Alex W: FYI — customer 'AcmePay' on Private deployment reporting intermittent 504s and our NLB target shows Unhealthy. They say this started after a config change. Can we triage?
Maria T: Thanks — can you paste the target group health check config and a sample host from their VPC? Also which LB type (NLB vs ALB)?
Alex W: It's NLB (internal) -> target group TCP healthcheck on :443 (healthy threshold 3, interval 10s). Target group output: 
```
Target 10.0.4.12:443 -> Unhealthy  (last_failure_reason: connection timeout)
Target 10.0.4.13:443 -> Healthy
```
Only one of their nodes shows Unhealthy. App logs show TLS handshake failures for the failed node.
Samir P: Ok. Two quick checks: 1) from their bastion, curl the IP:port and include SNI/Host to mimic the LB health check; 2) tcpdump on the target to see if packets from NLB node reach it. Example commands: 
```
curl -v --resolve api.acmepay.internal:443:10.0.4.12 https://api.acmepay.internal/health
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.4.12:443 -servername api.acmepay.internal
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 10.0.1.240 and port 443 -c 50
```
Maria T: Note: NLB TCP health checks do not send Host headers or SNI by default unless you configured TLS health checks with SNI. If customer expects SNI/Host-based virtual hosting, the target must handle default cert or SNI from the check.
Alex W: Ran the openssl test from bastion -> output shows handshake abort and cert CN mismatch: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
139786...: TLS alert number 40 (handshake failure)
---
subject=C = US, O = InternalServices, CN = service.internal
issuer=...
---
peer certificate CN=service.internal (expected api.acmepay.internal)
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 300 bytes
```
So their app presents a cert for `service.internal` which doesn't match the external SNI. The healthy node 10.0.4.13 returns the api cert. 
Karen L: Two likely causes: 1) host-based firewall or iptables dropping packets only from the NLB node(s) (ephemeral source ports), or 2) the node's virtual host config is wrong (wrong cert selected based on SNI). Also confirm NACLs allow return traffic and ephemeral ports. Ask customer to: 
- check iptables: `sudo iptables -L -n -v`
- check `ss -ntlp | grep 443` and the listener binding
- verify app/Envoy presents correct cert for both IPs (check SNI routing)
Samir P: If Envoy is used, common misconfig is `server_name` mismatch in TLS context or `require_sni` flagged. Example envoy snippet to look for: 
```
filter_chains:
  - filters: ...
    transport_socket:
      name: envoy.transport_sockets.tls
      typed_config:
        common_tls_context:
          tls_certificates: [{certificate_chain: {filename: "/etc/certs/api.pem"}}]
          sni: "api.acmepay.internal"
```
If the config only binds cert for `api.acmepay.internal` via SNI and the NLB healthcheck doesn't provide SNI, the default cert may be `service.internal`.
Alex W: Good catch. I checked with customer: host-based firewall on 10.0.4.12 was blocking packets from the NLB node IP range because they only whitelisted a small CIDR (10.0.1.0/28). NLB node IP is 10.0.1.240/32 so healthcheck packets were intermittent and sometimes triggered fallback path where Envoy served the wrong cert. They've adjusted iptables to allow the NLB node(s) and opened ephemeral port range in the NACL. They also updated Envoy to present a default cert that matches, not rely on SNI for healthcheck path.
Karen L: Great — please confirm post-change and ask them to run the healthcheck from inside after update. Also recommend they document in KB: 1) allow NLB node IPs + ephemeral ports, 2) ensure default TLS cert covers healthcheck or enable SNI on check.
Alex W: Customer confirmed targets now show Healthy and 504s stopped after changes. I'll follow up with a KB draft. :white_check_mark:
